paper_title: More Tokens, Lower Precision Towards the Optimal Token-Precision   Trade-off in KV Cache Compression
caption: The results of Layer-Wise Quantized Pruning on Mistral-7B-v0.2-Instruct, with SnapKV as pruning method. KV cache budget=1/64.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relative change in performance across different layers for various configurations of token- precision trade-offs in KV cache compression. The x-axis represents the layer ranges (Layer1-4, Layer5-12, Layer13-20, Layer21-28, Layer29-32), with a categorical scale. The y-axis is labeled "Relative Change" with a linear scale, ranging from -25% to 5%, with tick labels at intervals of 5%. The plot compares five different configurations: Baseline of 4×tokens, 4-bit (gray dashed line), LB-Avg of 2×tokens, 8-bit (yellow solid line with circle markers), RULER4k of 2×tokens, 8-bit (light blue solid line with square markers), LB-Avg of 1×tokens, 16-bit (red solid line with circle markers), and RULER4k of 1×tokens, 16-bit (dark blue solid line with square markers). The Baseline remains steady at 0% across all layer ranges. The LB-Avg of 2×tokens, 8-bit starts at approximately 0% and decreases to around -1% at Layer13-20 before rising back to 0% at Layer29-32. The RULER4k of 2×tokens, 8-bit begins at around -2%, decreases to approximately -13% at Layer13-20, and then increases to around -4% at Layer29-32. The LB-Avg of 1×tokens, 16-bit starts at approximately -1%, decreases to around -4% at Layer13-20, and then rises to around -1% at Layer29-32. The RULER4k of 1×tokens, 16-bit begins at around -3%, sharply decreases to approximately -25% at Layer13-20, and then increases to around -6% at Layer29-32.
